_comment: Statutory guidance that is revised on a schedule. Nothing here stores the content — only where
the current version lives. Editions are superseded (KCSIE every September; exclusions and RSHE
both changed in 2026), so a copy baked into the repo would go quietly wrong. The refresh job
resolves each canonical page and writes what it finds to Firestore kb_tier2/{id}, stamped with
when it was fetched, and the agent is told to say so.
Always link the canonical landing page, never a dated PDF filename: the PDF URL changes with
every edition, the landing page does not.

topics.title: Keeping Children Safe in Education
topics.why: The statutory safeguarding guidance every school follows. Referenced constantly; quoted wrongly at your peril.
topics.editionNote: A new edition normally comes into force on 1 September. Check which is current before relying on any detail.

topics.title: Suspension and permanent exclusion
topics.why: Sets the process and the language. Getting the terminology wrong here matters legally.
topics.editionNote: A revised version came into force on 26 July 2026 — seed from the current page, not from memory.

topics.title: Behaviour in schools
topics.why: The companion to the exclusions guidance; the vocabulary of behaviour policies.

topics.title: Relationships education, RSE and health education
topics.why: Statutory curriculum content, and a subject where being out of date is conspicuous.
topics.editionNote: Guidance published 15 July 2025 comes into force 1 September 2026.

topics.title: Ofsted report cards and grades
topics.why: The inspection scale changed in November 2025; the old one-word grades are gone.

topics.title: Working together to improve school attendance
topics.why: Registration codes and the escalation process. Codes must never be invented.

topics.title: School teachers' pay and conditions
topics.why: Directed time, PPA, pay ranges and TLRs. Revised annually, so figures date fast.

topics.title: Prevent duty guidance
topics.why: A statutory duty schools hold; background awareness rather than day-to-day planning.
